Partition

/par-TISH-un/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Partition means to divide something into two or more separate parts

Partition means to divide something into two or more separate parts. The landlord decided to partition the enormous loft into three smaller apartments, each with its own entrance.

Worked Example

Before installing a second operating system, Maya partitioned her laptop's hard drive into two sections so the systems could run without interfering with each other.

Maya divided one drive into separate, walled-off sections — the core idea of the verb. You can partition physical spaces, territories, or even digital storage; in every case, one whole becomes distinct parts.

How Partition Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

divide

divide: to split into parts

subdivide

subdivide: to divide into smaller parts

split

split: to break or separate into sections

Antonyms

unite

unite: to join into one

merge

merge: to combine into a single whole

How Strong Is It? — divide → fragment → partition

divide vs. partition

divide vs. partition: Divide is the plain, all-purpose word for splitting something up in any way at all.

fragment vs. partition

fragment vs. partition: Fragment goes further than partition — it suggests breaking something into many scattered pieces, often damaging its wholeness.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — part

Root — part: part, share (Latin pars, partis)

Suffix — -ition

Suffix — -ition: act or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Built on part + -ition, the word literally names the act of making parts — to partition something is to turn one whole into several separate parts.

Use the root in a new word: impartial

Use the root in a new word: impartial: A referee must stay impartial, refusing to take either side's part in the dispute.

Word Choice

neutral / structural & geographic

This card teaches partition as a verb — the action of dividing a space, territory, or system into sections (you partition a room, a country, a hard drive). The related noun (a partition = the physical divider itself) exists but is secondary here. Compare segregation, also in this unit: partition divides one thing into parts; segregation keeps groups of people or animals apart from each other.
